'''Libgcrypt''' is a cryptography library developed as a separated module of [[GnuPG]].<ref>{{cite mailing list
| last=Koch
| first=Werner
| url=https://lists.gnupg.org/pipermail/gnupg-devel/1998-December/015041.html
| title=libgcrypt
| publisher=gnupg-devel
| date=1998-12-04
| accessdate=2017-08-30}}</ref>
It can also be used independently of GnuPG, but depends on its error-reporting library Libgpg-error.<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://gnupg.org/software/libgpg-error/index.html
| title=Libgpg-error
| work=GnuPG software
| date=2017-03-22
| accessdate=2017-12-13}}</ref>

Libgcrypt features its own [[Arbitrary-precision arithmetic|''multiple precision arithmetic'']] implementation, with assembler implementations for a variety of processors, including Alpha, AMD64, HP PA-RISC, i386, i586, M68K, MIPS 3, PowerPC, and SPARC.  It also features an ''[[Entropy (computing)|entropy]] gathering'' utility, coming in different versions for Unix-like and Windows machines.

Usually multiple, stable branches of Libgcrypt are maintained in parallel; as of May 2026 this is the Libgrypt 1.12 branch as [[Long-term support|LTS ("long-term support")]] branch, the 1.11 branch as previous [[Software release life cycle#Stable release|stable]] branch, which will be maintained at least until 2028-06-30<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://gnupg.org/download/#end-of-life
| title=End-of-life dates for GnuPG and Libgcrypt
| work=GnuPG software
| date=2026-05-14
| accessdate=2026-05-14}}</ref>
, and the 1.8 branch as "old-LTS" branch, which is still maintained as long a customer with an "extended Long Term Support contract" exists, despite its original [[Software release life cycle#End-of-life|end-of-life]] date being 2024-12-31.
